exposure: Presence or absence of indications for cesarean delivery
outcome: Risk of obesity (based on International Obesity Task Force or World Health Organization body mass index cutoffs)
cohort: 22,068 offspring born to 15,271 women, followed up via questionnaire
finding: Cesarean birth was associated with an increased risk of obesity in offspring, even after adjusting for major confounding factors.
mod_finding: Offspring born via vaginal birth after a previous cesarean delivery had a lower risk of obesity compared to those born to women with repeated cesarean deliveries.
